we have presented a new numerical scheme for the Ericksen–Leslie model of nematic liquid crystal hydrodynamics, and that the scheme has been used to study the annihilation of a topological defect pair in a nematic liquid crystal flow.

the dynamics of defect motion in nematic liquid crystal flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the annihilation of a pair is not a symmetric process and the stretching parameter in transport equation is a major contributor to the asymmetry of the process.
the annihilation of hedgehog-antipole pair in hydrodynamical nematic liquid crystal flow is a very complicated process.
the annihilation speed of a pair of hedgehog-antiparticle depends strongly on the type of transport, the elastic properties of the material, and the initial conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new mathematical model for the dynamics of defect motion and presented an ecient numerical scheme for solving the nonlinear system of equations.
the annihilation of a pair is faster in the case of elastic transport than in the case of hydrodynamic transport.
we are able to numerically simulate the dynamics of a hedgehog and an antihedgehog pair annihilating each other in the hydrodynamic theory of nematic liquid crystals.

the dynamics of defect annihilation can be controlled by the choice of transport equation in the model.
the dynamics of defect annihilation can be controlled by the transport equation of the directional order parameters.
